title: Data labeling cleanup notes - draft
content:
Notes / scratchpad for data cleanup and label guideline updates (working draft)

Purpose:
- Consolidate edge cases we've been flagging in the last 2 sprints.
- Propose concrete labeling rules and examples for ambiguous items.
- Create a short QA checklist for reviewers doing cleanup passes.

Context / background:
- Observed an uptick in inconsistent labels across the same intent/entity types — especially in multi-turn examples and snippets with code or quoted text.
- Cleanup ticket: JIRA DL-234 tracks the high-priority batches.
- Slack discussion: #data-labeling (thread started by Asha on 2024-01-08) with sample disagreements attached.

High-level rules (proposal):
1) Prefer specificity where possible (use most specific intent available). If uncertain, use AMBIGUOUS intent tag and add reason in the comment field.
2) Multi-label allowed only when the example clearly expresses >1 independent intents (e.g., "Remind me to call mom and what's the weather?" -> REMINDER + WEATHER_QUERY).
3) Entities: annotate canonical forms where possible ("3pm" -> TIME:15:00). If entity is fuzzy ("sometime tomorrow"), annotate as TIME with attribute=fuzzy (comment).
4) Model-generated vs user-provided content: mark SOURCE=MODEL if there is explicit evidence (system field or generation token). Otherwise treat as USER. We need an automated flagging script (see github PR).

Edge cases and suggested handling (examples):
- Quoted speech inside a user message:
  Example: User: "He said, "I don't care."" -> Label the outer message for intent (e.g., REPORT) and do not create a separate label for the inner quoted sentence unless instruction asks to extract quoted content.

- Sarcasm / implied sentiment:
  Example: "Nice job, genius." -> Intent: SARCASM? We don't have a sentiment breakdown here; mark as AMBIGUOUS_INTENT + add reviewer note: sarcasm suspected. If task requires sentiment, add explicit SENTIMENT label per sentiment guidelines.

- Code blocks and technical snippets:
  Example: "Here's the error: 
```Traceback (Most recent call last): ...```" -> Intent: DEBUG/ERROR_REPORT. Entities: CODE_SNIPPET present. Do NOT label internal code tokens as PII unless there's an obvious secret (API keys, tokens).

- Multiple languages / non-English text:
  - If majority is non-English, set LANGUAGE tag and only label intents if annotator is confident. Otherwise mark as LANG_UNKNOWN and AMBIGUOUS. We should route these to bilingual annotators.

- PII ambiguous cases:
  Example: "My number is 555-1234" with missing area code -> label as PII_PHONE but add note: partial. If it's clearly fake (555-prefix common placeholder), mark as PII_PLACEHOLDER and do not redact in dataset; add flag for downstream policies.

- Partial conversations (no system prompt/context):
  - If an utterance relies on prior turns for intent, mark CONTEXT_REQUIRED. Add reviewer comment indicating what context is missing.

- System prompts / instructions present in text field:
  - If the dataset item includes an assistant/system prompt, annotate it separately with ROLE=SYSTEM and do not mix with user intent labels.

Sample labeling table (for reviewer reference) - plain text examples:
1) "What's the weather tomorrow in SF?" -> Intent: WEATHER_QUERY; Entities: LOCATION:San Francisco; TIME:tomorrow
2) "Remind me to call Mom at 3pm" -> Intent: SET_REMINDER; Entities: CONTACT:Mom; TIME:15:00
3) "I want a refund, this product sucks" -> Intent: CUSTOMER_COMPLAINT; Entities: PRODUCT:unknown (if product name missing). If profanity present, add TOXICity flag only when the labelling task includes safety.
4) "Can you write me a python function to parse csv?" -> Intent: CODE_REQUEST; Entities: LANGUAGE:python; TOPIC:csv parsing
5) "He said it was trash" -> Intent: AMBIGUOUS (could be item review or reference to earlier comment); mark CONTEXT_REQUIRED

Reviewer QA checklist for cleanup pass:
- [ ] Check for consistent intent across obvious paraphrases (search for duplicates in batch).
- [ ] Verify entity canonicalization (times, dates, normalized places).
- [ ] Confirm multi-turn items have CONTEXT_REQUIRED flagged if prior turns are missing.
- [ ] Ensure model-generated items are marked SOURCE=MODEL where applicable.
- [ ] Add a short comment for any AMBIGUOUS labels explaining the ambiguity.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Do we want a separate label for sarcasm vs marking as AMBIGUOUS? (Discuss with product; pinging @product-hosted-api).
- Build a small validation script that checks for conflicting labels in the same example (e.g., intent=WEATHER_QUERY and intent=ORDER_STATUS). See github:inference/labeling-scripts PR#78 for starter code.
- Route non-English examples to bilingual annotators — need to update the workflow in Confluence page (confluence:DL-annotation-guidelines).

Cleanup plan (next steps):
1) Run automated normalization (times, dates, phone formats) via labeling-scripts. Ryan to own (JIRA DL-240).
2) Do two reviewer passes on the top 5k noisy examples flagged by model disagreement metric (see DL-234).
3) Update the short guideline doc (this file) and convert to a one-pager for the annotation UI as quick help.

Notes to self (Maya):
- When doing the manual pass, keep a quick diff of changed labels per annotator (we want to measure annotator drift).
- Save common ambiguous phrasing list to shared spreadsheet for sampling.

Comments from collaborators (copied from Slack thread):
- Asha: "We should be stricter about multi-intent — only allow when both intents are actionable separately."
- Ryan: "I'll add a quick script to flag likely model-generated samples based on prompt tokens."

End of draft. Will iterate after the first cleanup pass and team sync on 2024-02-20.
